_: Copy to config.json and edit. Every key below is optional except host: drop the ones you do not want to override and config.py's default applies. Keys starting with _ are ignored, so this line can stay. null means 'use the default'.
__deployment: systemd. The unit names below are the labels of record: they name the files under /etc/systemd/system and they are what systemctl is given. All four (live_unit is further down) must differ from each other. run_as_user is required -- an empty systemd User= is not an error, it just runs the unit as root, which is what these units exist to avoid. See deploy/systemd/ and deploy/pi/.
__retention: keep_days deletes *.bin.gz on rotation -- which is the exact form sync.py uploads, so an hour pruned before its upload succeeded is gone for good. 7 is right for a Pi on a thumb drive WITH uploads working: it bounds the drive at about 15 MB of records and leaves a week of margin against a network outage. Set it to 0, keeping everything, if the archive on this host is the only copy. config.py's default is 0 for exactly that reason. See FINDINGS 40.
__watching: There is deliberately nothing here for the watchdog or for rediscovery. Both are configured OUTSIDE this file, on purpose. The notification target lives in alert.conf beside this file, mode 600 and gitignored, because an ntfy topic is a capability rather than a name -- anyone holding it can read the alerts and post to them -- and this repository is public; see alerts.py. Rediscovery is a `log.py --discover` flag on the unit's ExecStart, not a setting, because a LAN sweep is not something a logger should do to somebody's network unless they asked for it in the command that starts it. The staleness threshold is likewise `bin/watchdog.py --stale-after`, in deploy/systemd/sigen-watchdog.service.template.
__offsite: sync.py, the offsite copy. It is the only path the data has -- there is no local viewer -- so on this deployment it is not optional and sync_enabled must be true. It needs boto3, which on a Pi comes from `sudo apt install python3-boto3` and NOT from pip (Debian refuses pip install --user with 'externally-managed-environment'). Credentials come from a named ~/.aws profile, NEVER from this file; deploy/pi/provision.sh pushes just that one profile over SSH. The uploader sends rotated .bin.gz and manifests only, never the open .bin, so the current hour reaches S3 on the next rotation.
__live: live.py, the live stream: log.py offers each archived record to it over a Unix datagram socket (fire-and-forget; the archive never waits for it and it adds no reads of the device), and it publishes seven metrics to AWS IoT Core every tick. Off here and by default, because it needs a cloud stack and a certificate first; the Pi's own config.json sets it true. live_endpoint is the account's IoT data endpoint, host only, from `aws iot describe-endpoint --endpoint-type iot:Data-ATS`. The certificate and key are FILES, by default in live-cert/ beside this file as certificate.pem.crt and private.pem.key; deploy/pi/provision.sh pushes them mode 600 and they are gitignored. Nothing in this block can stop the logger starting: it is checked by `live.py --check`, not by config.py. It needs paho-mqtt, from `sudo apt install python3-paho-mqtt`. See cloud/README.md.
